title: Samurai removal 6 of 7: a one-time safe cleanup of Samurai's leftover data, with a notice of what was kept
story: On the first start after Samurai's removal, Maestro quietly deletes Samurai's old files: audit logs, run records, schedule and latches, journal, harvest reports, its two settings files and its hand-over folders. A run worktree is removed only when its work is on the default branch, no saved terminal reopens it, and its only extra files are Samurai's own notes or build output; any other worktree is kept and listed in a new closeable bottom-left notice. This replaces the earlier runbook line that Samurai files on disk are left where they are.

checks.criterion: A kept run worktree is listed in one closeable notice
checks.steps: In a fresh test copy of Maestro, make a git repo 'demo-project' on main with one commit; add worktree 'demo-wt' on branch 'demo-run' with one committed file; write runs/demo-project-0123456789ab/demo.json in Maestro's data folder with project_path, worktree_path, epic, status ACTIVE and created_at; make sure there is no 'samurai-cleanup-done' file; start Maestro.
checks.expected: A bottom-left 'Samurai cleanup' card shows the demo-wt path with 'unmerged commits'; × closes it; demo-wt is still on disk.

checks.criterion: With nothing kept there is no notice, and later starts do nothing
checks.steps: With no run records, start Maestro, then start it again.
checks.expected: No notice either time, and a 'samurai-cleanup-done' file exists in Maestro's data folder.
